title: Jump, jump, jump!
summary: We can jump in many ways. Jumping makes our bodies strong and is fun when we play safely.
body:
## Ways of jumping

- **Two feet together**: bend your knees, swing your arms and jump forward.
- **Jump up high**: reach for the sky like you want to touch a mango.
- **Jump over a line**: draw a line on the ground and jump over it, forward and back.
- **Star jump**: jump and open your arms and legs like a star ⭐.

## Jumping with things around us

You can **improvise** (make your own) things to jump with:

- A rope or a long strip of cloth for skipping
- Sticks laid on the ground to jump over
- Old sacks for a sack race

## Jumping songs

Sing while you jump to keep time. Try counting: *"One, two, three, jump!"*

## Stay safe

- Jump on soft, flat ground with no stones or glass.
- Leave space between you and your friends.
- Land softly with bent knees.
activities:
1. Do 5 jumps with two feet together. Then 5 star jumps.
2. Lay two sticks on the ground and jump over them forward and backward.
3. Sing a song you know and jump to its beat.
reflection: Which jump was the most fun for you? Why?

quiz.question: Where is it safe to jump?
options: On flat ground with no stones

quiz.question: How should you land after a jump?
What can you use to make a skipping rope?
In a star jump, your arms and legs...

title: Hello! Sounds, letters and greetings
summary: Every letter makes a sound. We use words to greet people kindly every day.
body:
## Letters make sounds

Every letter has a **sound**. Say them with your teacher or parent:

- **a** says /a/ as in **a**pple
- **b** says /b/ as in **b**all
- **c** says /k/ as in **c**at
- **m** says /m/ as in **m**ama

Put your hand on your throat and say /m/. Can you feel it buzz?

## Greeting people

When we meet someone, we **greet** them. Greeting shows we care.

| Time | We say |
|---|---|
| Morning | **Good morning!** |
| Afternoon | **Good afternoon!** |
| Evening | **Good evening!** |
| Any time | **Hello! How are you?** |

When someone greets you, answer: **"I am fine, thank you."**

When you leave, say **"Goodbye!"** or **"See you tomorrow!"**
activities:
1. Greet three people at home today. Use the right greeting for the time of day.
2. Find three things at home that start with the /b/ sound (ball, bed, bag...). Say each one aloud.
3. Play a game: one person says a sound, the other names something that starts with it.
reflection: How do you feel when someone greets you with a smile?

quiz.question: What do we say when we meet someone in the morning?
Which word starts with the /b/ sound?
Someone asks, 'How are you?' What do you answer?
What do we say when we are leaving?

title: Keeping my body clean
summary: A clean body keeps us healthy. We clean our face, teeth, hands, feet and hair every day.
body:
## Why we keep clean

Dirt carries **germs**. Germs are too small to see, but they can make us sick. When we keep our body clean, we stay healthy and feel fresh.

## How we clean each part

| Part of the body | What we use | When |
|---|---|---|
| **Hands** | Water and soap | Before eating, after the toilet, after playing |
| **Face** | Water, soap and a clean towel | Morning and evening |
| **Teeth** | Toothbrush and toothpaste (or a chewing stick, *mswaki*) | After breakfast and before bed |
| **Feet** | Water and soap | Every evening |
| **Hair** | Water, soap and a comb | Wash it often, comb it every day |

## Washing hands the right way

1. Wet your hands with clean water.
2. Rub soap on both hands, between the fingers and under the nails.
3. Count to 20 while you scrub.
4. Rinse with clean water and dry with a clean cloth.

No soap? Ash and clean water also help remove dirt.
activities:
1. Wash your hands the right way and count to 20 while scrubbing.
2. Draw a toothbrush and a bar of soap. Colour them.
3. Make a chart with a parent: tick each time you brush your teeth this week.
reflection: Which part of your body do you sometimes forget to clean? How will you remember?

quiz.question: When should we wash our hands?
options: Before eating and after the toilet

quiz.question: What do we use to clean our teeth?
Why do we keep our bodies clean?
How long should you scrub your hands with soap?

title: Maamkuzi na maagano
summary: Tunawasalimu watu kwa heshima. Tunatumia maneno ya maamkuzi tunapokutana na ya maagano tunapoachana.
body:
## Maamkuzi

Tunapokutana na mtu, tunamwamkua. Kuamkua ni kuonyesha **heshima** na **upendo**.

| Tunasema | Jibu |
|---|---|
| **Hujambo?** | **Sijambo.** |
| **Hamjambo?** (kwa watu wengi) | **Hatujambo.** |
| **Habari yako?** | **Nzuri.** |
| **Shikamoo** (kwa mtu mzima) | **Marahaba.** |

Tunamwamkua mtu mzima kwa heshima. Tunasema **"Shikamoo"**, naye anajibu **"Marahaba"**.

## Maagano

Tunapoachana, tunaagana:

- **Kwaheri!** — jibu: **Kwaheri!**
- **Kwaherini!** (kwa watu wengi)
- **Tutaonana kesho!**
- **Usiku mwema!** (tunapokwenda kulala)
activities:
1. Mwamkue mama, baba au mlezi wako asubuhi ya leo kwa Kiswahili.
2. Igiza na rafiki: mmoja anaamkua, mwingine anajibu.
3. Sema "Usiku mwema" kwa watu wa nyumbani kabla ya kulala.
reflection: Kwa nini ni vizuri kumwamkua mtu mzima kwa heshima?

quiz.question: Mtu akisema 'Hujambo?' unajibu nini?
Tunasema nini kwa mtu mzima tunapomwamkua?
Mtu mzima anajibu 'Shikamoo' kwa kusema...
Tunasema nini tunapoachana na rafiki?

title: Sorting, matching and patterns
summary: Before counting, we learn to sort things into groups, match things that are alike, order them and make patterns.
body:
## Sorting

To **sort** is to put things that are alike into one group. We can sort by:

- **Colour** — all red beans here, all white beans there
- **Size** — big stones and small stones
- **Shape** — round bottle tops and square boxes

## Matching

To **match** is to find things that go together: a cup and its saucer, a shoe and its pair, a pot and its lid.

## Ordering

We can put things in **order**: from the smallest to the biggest, or from the shortest to the tallest.

🐜 → 🐓 → 🐐 → 🐄 (small to big)

## Patterns

A **pattern** repeats again and again.

🔴 🔵 🔴 🔵 🔴 🔵 ...

What comes next? **🔴**

You can make patterns with leaves, bottle tops, stones or claps: *clap, stamp, clap, stamp...*
activities:
1. Collect 10 bottle tops or beans. Sort them by colour.
2. Line up 4 cups or sticks from the shortest to the longest.
3. Make a pattern with leaves and stones: leaf, stone, leaf, stone. Ask someone what comes next.
reflection: Where at home do people sort things? (Think of washing clothes or putting away utensils.)

quiz.question: What comes next? red, blue, red, blue, red, ...
Which goes with a shoe?
Which animal is the biggest?
Putting red beans in one group and white beans in another is called...
